message.content:
**Answer:** The sculpture most frequently cited as the iconic masterpiece of the 19th century is **Auguste Rodin’s “The Kiss” (1889)**. --- ### Why “The Kiss” is considered the 19th‑century icon | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840–1917) | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist, early modernism | | **Material** | Bronze (originally a plaster study) | | **Location** | Multiple casts worldwide – the original is in the Musée Rodin, Paris; a prominent cast sits in the Rodin Museum, Philadelphia. | | **Cultural Impact** | • Became a symbol of romantic love and human intimacy.
• Influenced the transition from classical idealism to expressive realism.
• Its dramatic pose and emotional depth captured the public imagination and earned Rodin international acclaim. | --- ### Other contenders | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Why it’s notable | |-----------|--------|------|------------------| | **“The Gates of Hell”** | Rodin | 1880–1917 (unfinished) | Massive bronze portal inspired by Dante; a monumental statement of modern sculpture. | | **“The Thinker”** | Rodin | 1902 (first cast) | Though technically early 20th, it became the most reproduced and recognized sculpture worldwide. | | **“Statue of Liberty”** | Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi | 1886 | Monumental bronze sculpture symbolizing freedom; a national icon. | | **“The Venus de Milo”** (recast) | Various | 200 BC (original) – 19th‑century casts | Classic Greek marble revived in the 19th‑century through casts and reproductions. | --- ### Bottom line While several 19th‑century works have left a lasting legacy, **Rodin’s “The Kiss”** stands out as the most celebrated and widely recognized sculpture of that era, embodying the shift toward modern artistic expression and capturing the public’s imagination in a way that few other works of the time have matched.
